method_card.title: How to Add, Subtract, Multiply and Divide Fractions
steps: Convert any mixed numbers to improper fractions first.
To add or subtract: find a common denominator, then combine the tops only.
To multiply: multiply tops and bottoms. To divide: keep, flip, multiply.
Always simplify the final fraction by its highest common factor.
method_card.content:
Adding and subtracting needs a common denominator: convert both fractions so the bottoms match, then combine the tops only.

Multiplying needs no common denominator: multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Cross-cancel first to keep numbers small.

Dividing uses keep, flip, multiply: keep the first fraction, flip the second, then multiply.

Mixed numbers must become improper fractions before you calculate. Simplify every answer at the end.

problem_bank.bronze_description: Add, subtract or multiply two simple fractions, then simplify the answer.
problem_bank.silver_description: Divide fractions with keep, flip, multiply, and handle a mixed number or an unlike denominator.
problem_bank.gold_description: Combine mixed numbers, three fractions or a BIDMAS chain, converting and simplifying throughout.

bronze.title: Bronze: adding, subtracting and multiplying simple fractions
steps: For + or −: give both fractions the same denominator, then combine the tops only.
For ×: no common denominator is needed. Multiply the tops together and the bottoms together.
Always simplify the final fraction by dividing top and bottom by their highest common factor.

steps.label: Common denominator
steps.content: The LCD of 6 and 2 is 6, so 1/2 = 3/6.

steps.label: Check
steps.content: 2/3 turned back into sixths is 4/6, matching the sum.

silver.title: Silver: dividing fractions and using mixed numbers
steps: To divide, use keep, flip, multiply: keep the first fraction, flip the second, then multiply across.
Turn any mixed number into an improper fraction before you calculate.
Multiply or add as usual, then simplify the answer.

gold.title: Gold: mixed numbers, three fractions and BIDMAS
steps: Convert every mixed number to an improper fraction before you start.
For a chain of fractions, give them all one common denominator, then combine the tops in order.
With mixed operations, follow BIDMAS: do division and multiplication before addition and subtraction. Simplify at the end.

steps.label: Check
steps.content: A number times a fraction just under a half of 3 lands on 1; 3/2 × 2/3 cancels to 1.

steps.say: Forget the maths for a second. Picture a pizza cut into quarter-slices.

steps.pre: You eat one half of the pizza. How many quarter-slices is that?
steps.hint: A half of the pizza is the same as two of the quarter-slices.

steps.say: Your friend then eats one more quarter-slice.

steps.pre: Altogether, how many quarter-slices have gone?
steps.hint: Your 2 quarters plus your friend's 1 quarter.

steps.say: You just worked out \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\) without any rules. The trick was turning the half into quarters so both pieces were the same size. That is exactly what find a common denominator means: make the slices match, then count them.
